name: Splinter Grath
geological_features: Angular, fractured terrain suggesting the body is a remnant of a larger planetesimal
Deep impact craters exposing layered mineral strata in cross-section
A massive fissure bisecting the body along its longest axis
specific_features: Irregular rotation producing unpredictable day-night thermal extremes
Exposed veins of crystallized platinum visible in the walls of the axial fissure
description: Splinter Grath is barely a world at all, a jagged, irregular chunk of rock and metal just under seven hundred kilometers across, tumbling through space on an erratic axis. Its surface is a shattered moonscape of angular ridges, deep impact craters, and fractured plains that suggest it was once part of something much larger, blown apart by a cataclysmic collision in the system's violent youth. The great axial fissure splits the body nearly in half, a canyon so deep it exposes the differentiated layers of the original parent body.

With no atmosphere to moderate temperatures, Splinter Grath swings between scorching sunlit faces and shadow-side cold deep enough to freeze carbon dioxide solid. The silence on the surface is absolute. There is no wind, no geological activity, no sound of any kind, only the slow tick of thermal expansion and contraction cracking rock at the molecular level across millions of years.

Survey teams flagged Splinter Grath as a mining prospect after spectral analysis revealed dense platinum deposits exposed by the axial fissure, essentially pre-excavated ore requiring minimal extraction effort. The body's low gravity makes bulk material transport relatively simple, and its location in the system's outer asteroid belt places it within reach of existing shipping lanes. Three mining claims have been filed, though none have yet been activated.

The primary challenge is the body's irregular rotation, which creates unpredictable thermal cycling that stresses equipment and makes surface operations a scheduling nightmare. Autonomous extraction platforms are the favored approach, though even those require hardening against the temperature swings. For now, Splinter Grath tumbles on in silence, its platinum veins glinting in the intermittent sunlight, waiting for the economics of extraction to tip in its favor.
